nodes.description: Biallelic germline CLDN14 variants, mostly missense with founder frameshift and missense alleles in Pakistan and a founder missense allele in Newfoundland, remove claudin-14 from tight-junction strands. Expressed in L fibroblasts, wild-type claudin-14 forms tight junctions while the p.Val85Asp and p.Gly101Arg mutants do not, and the two mutants differ in whether they reach the plasma membrane, so different alleles disable the protein by different routes.

nodes.description: Knockout mice are deaf, with a normal endocochlear potential, rapid outer hair cell degeneration and slower inner hair cell degeneration during the first three weeks of life.

In the one reported DFNB29 implant recipient, cochlear implantation improved sound-field thresholds but not speech discrimination. The implant bypasses the lost hair cells but depends on the auditory nerve, whose fibres and central connections are affected in Cldn14-null mice; whether that explains the poor discrimination is not known.

nodes.description: In Cldn14-null mice, inner hair cell ribbon synapses degenerate in apical regions from postnatal day 12, before the inner hair cells themselves are lost. Peripheral auditory nerve processes regress, especially the outer radial fibres, while spiral ganglion neuron density is unchanged. Centrally, the dorsal cochlear nucleus is smaller and glutamatergic input to the ventral cochlear nucleus is reduced. These changes in auditory nerve connectivity bear on how well a cochlear implant can work, and they have not been examined in patients.

nodes.description: Claudin-14 sits in the tight junctions between hair cells and supporting cells at the reticular lamina, which separate potassium-rich endolymph from sodium-rich perilymph. It makes these junctions restrictive to cations: expressed in MDCK monolayers it raises transepithelial resistance six-fold by lowering paracellular cation permeability. Without it the barrier is expected to leak cations. What this node is not: a failure of the endocochlear potential, which is normal in Cldn14-null mice, so the stria vascularis route that many other recessive deafness genes take is not involved.
